subject.title: [Bug]: `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` breaks `openai-codex` auth/keychain paths on macOS and can fail fresh runtime launch with `SecItemCopyMatching failed -50`

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the macOS service `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` default and add a narrower no-keychain or no-system-CA auth boundary, or change the macOS Node TLS default?
rationale: The reporter's bundled-CA workaround identifies the trigger, but the current macOS default protects launchd TLS behavior and the safest product boundary requires maintainer intent plus live macOS proof.

options.title: Scoped auth/runtime mitigation
options.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default and make the affected Codex auth/runtime launch paths avoid keychain/system-CA conflict with focused macOS coverage.

options.title: Rollback the macOS CA default
options.body: Disable or narrow `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` for macOS services, accepting the risk that launchd TLS behavior regresses unless proven otherwise.

options.title: Treat as unsupported environment
options.body: Document that `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` with Codex keychain auth is unsupported and rely on bundled-CA user workarounds.

recommendation.title: Scoped auth/runtime mitigation
recommendation.body: Keep the macOS service TLS default and make the affected Codex auth/runtime launch paths avoid keychain/system-CA conflict with focused macOS coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision most directly affects Codex auth and external CLI credential handling, where this history is strongest.
